name: APT17
affiliation_detail:
Intrusion Truth published a series of articles in July 2019 identifying APT17 as being managed by the Jinan bureau of the Chinese Ministry of State Security (MSS). They identified four individuals: (1) Guo Lin (郭林), assessed to be an MSS officer who is affiliated with four private technology companies in Jinan, (2) Wang Qingwei (王庆卫), (3) Zeng Xiaoyong (曾小勇, aka "envymask") and (4) Zhang Peng (aka "missll"). All identified individuals operated from Jinan, the capital of Shandong Province.
Intrusion Truth further documented links between APT17 operators and APT41, noting shared malware (BLACKCOFFEE) and personal connections between individuals, suggesting an "interlinked network of Chinese cyber actors sharing malware, expertise and connections."
No DOJ indictment has been filed against APT17 operators as of the profile date.
description:
APT17 is linked by Intrusion Truth to the Ministry of State Security's Jinan bureau (Shandong Province).
APT17 is characterized by prolific use of zero-day exploits (particularly Internet Explorer vulnerabilities), strategic web compromises (watering holes), and supply chain attacks. The group gained its "DeputyDog" name from FireEye's 2013 discovery of a campaign using IE zero-days against Japanese targets. Subsequent FireEye research documented Operation Ephemeral Hydra (2013) and Operation SnowMan (2014), both sharing infrastructure and tradecraft with DeputyDog. 
APT17 was, among other campaigns, described to be involved in the 2009 Operation Aurora. The group is also linked to the 2017 CCleaner supply chain compromise, which affected 2.27 million users and deployed the ShadowPad backdoor to a targeted subset. Most recently, in 2024, APT17 was observed targeting Italian companies and government entities with the 9002 RAT. 
Intrusion Truth reported that in 2015, during Xi Jinping's crackdown on Chinese hackers, a Jinan office associated with APT17 activity was raided by the local Public Security Bureau, resulting in several arrests. Intrusion Truth noted these arrests may have been used to co-opt hackers into MSS service, as APT17 activity continued.

campaigns.name: Operation Aurora
campaigns.description: Cyber espionage campaign targeting Google, Adobe, Juniper Networks, and 30+ other major companies. Attackers used a zero-day in Internet Explorer (CVE-2010-0249) to deliver the Hydraq/9002 RAT. Google disclosed the attack publicly in January 2010, stating attackers sought access to Gmail accounts of Chinese human rights activists and stole intellectual property including source code. The attack fundamentally changed public awareness of state-sponsored cyber espionage. Symantec attributed the attack to the "Elderwood" group (named after a source-code variable), which has been linked to APT17. McAfee named the campaign "Aurora" after a folder name found in the malware.

campaigns.name: Bit9 Breach
campaigns.description: Attackers compromised application whitelisting security firm Bit9, deploying HiKit rootkit variants and stealing digital code-signing certificates. The stolen certificates were subsequently used to sign malware in later campaigns, including the VOHO campaign. FireEye linked the Bit9 C2 infrastructure to Operation DeputyDog via shared domain registrations and IP addresses.

campaigns.name: Operation DeputyDog
campaigns.description: FireEye discovered a campaign using IE zero-day CVE-2013-3893 against Japanese organizations. Malware samples contained the builder string "DGGYDSYRL" — the basis for the "DeputyDog" name. Payloads were XOR-encoded (key 0x95) and disguised as image files. FireEye linked the C2 infrastructure to the Bit9 breach via shared domains (yahooeast.net, blankchair.com) and IP addresses. Most samples were compiled on 2013-08-19 within one second of each other.

sources.title: Operation DeputyDog: Zero-Day Attack Against Japanese Targets

campaigns.name: Operation Ephemeral Hydra
campaigns.description: FireEye discovered a new IE zero-day (CVE-2013-3918) deployed via strategic web compromise of a site "likely to draw visitors interested in national and international security policy." The attack was notable for loading its payload (9002 RAT variant) directly into memory without writing to disk — a technique not typically used by APT actors at the time. Infrastructure overlap with DeputyDog confirmed via the shared domain dll.freshdns.org.

campaigns.name: Operation SnowMan
campaigns.description: FireEye identified IE 10 zero-day CVE-2014-0322 served from the U.S. Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW.org) website as a watering hole targeting U.S. military personnel. The attack was timed during a paralyzing snowstorm at the U.S. Capitol ahead of Presidents' Day weekend. A Flash object orchestrated exploitation, dropping a ZxShell backdoor via the same 0x95 XOR/.jpg extension technique used in DeputyDog. Websense also identified targeting of GIFAS (French aerospace association). Infrastructure and tradecraft links confirmed connection to DeputyDog and Ephemeral Hydra campaigns.

campaigns.name: Operation SMN (Industry Coalition vs. Axiom)
campaigns.description: Coordinated industry coalition led by Novetta (with Symantec, Cisco, FireEye, F-Secure, iSIGHT Partners, Microsoft, ThreatConnect, Tenable, ThreatTrack Security, Volexity) targeting the Axiom group's malware infrastructure. The coalition shared intelligence and resources to create comprehensive, multi-vendor detection for Hikit, ZxShell, Derusbi, Winnti, and other Axiom tools. This was one of the first major cross-industry coordinated responses to a state-sponsored APT group.

sources.title: Operation SMN: Axiom Threat Actor Group Report

campaigns.name: BLACKCOFFEE/TechNet Dead Drop Resolver
campaigns.description: FireEye and Microsoft jointly exposed APT17's technique of creating bogus profiles on Microsoft TechNet and embedding encoded C2 IP addresses in profile pages and forum posts for BLACKCOFFEE malware variants. The group created biographical sections and posted in legitimate threads to make profiles appear authentic. This "dead drop resolver" technique made it difficult for defenders to identify true C2 locations and allowed infrastructure to remain active longer. Microsoft released anti-malware signatures; FireEye released IOCs.

campaigns.name: CCleaner Supply Chain Compromise
campaigns.description: Attackers compromised Piriform's network (CCleaner developer, acquired by Avast July 2017) and injected a backdoor into CCleaner version 5.33.6162, affecting approximately 2.27 million users who downloaded the compromised update. Kaspersky's Costin Raiu first identified code overlap between the CCleaner backdoor and Axiom/APT17 tools. Intezer confirmed shared code with earlier APT17 samples. Avast's investigation found ShadowPad backdoor installed on four Piriform computers (April 2017), with custom-built keylogger capabilities. The second-stage payload was deployed to only ~40 machines, targeting major tech companies. Attackers initially entered Piriform's network via TeamViewer. In 2019, Avast detected and thwarted a second supply chain attack attempt against CCleaner, again attributed to Axiom/APT17.

campaigns.name: Italian Government and Companies (9002 RAT)
campaigns.description: Italian cybersecurity firm TG Soft documented APT17 targeting Italian companies and government entities in two waves. The first campaign (June 24) used a malicious Office document; the second (July 2) used a link. Both invited victims to install a fake Skype for Business package from a domain mimicking the Italian government, delivering a variant of the 9002 RAT. The RAT was deployed via an MSI installer that triggered a JAR file through VBScript, which decrypted and executed shellcode launching 9002 RAT. The malware included diskless variants and modular architecture to reduce detection.

sources.title: China-linked APT17 Targets Italian Companies with 9002 RAT Malware
